identity.method: Exact COL26.8 accepted species usage, including verbatim scientific name and authorship, rank, status, sourceDatasetId, and higher classification, verified against the pinned registry search record.
identity.scope: Nominal species as represented by COL26.8 usage 3F8JD. The biological evidence below concerns one laboratory microcosm comparison and does not establish variation among wild populations or a complete species concept.

lifeStatusScope.wild: The selected paper identifies G. pulex as native in the U.K.; its laboratory microcosms do not measure wild population dynamics or field rates.
lifeStatusScope.domesticated: Domestication has not been assessed; laboratory experiments are not treated as domestication.
lifeStatusScope.fossil: Fossil occurrence and geological age have not been assessed.

sources.title: Fincham et al. (2023), Interactive effects of resource quality and temperature drive differences in detritivory among native and invasive freshwater amphipods
sources.version: Freshwater Biology 68(6):915-925; version of record first published 2023-03-30
sources.license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), verified in the repository record for the published version
sources.scope: Primary laboratory microcosm comparison of one U.K. native amphipod and two invasive Dikerogammarus species across three temperature treatments and three leaf diets; only the abstract result about relative detrital processing is paraphrased.
sources.rightsHolder: William N. W. Fincham, Lee E. Brown, Helen E. Roy, and Alison M. Dunn
sources.licenseAppliesTo: Published article under the stated CC BY 4.0 license. No figures, tables, or deposited datasets are reused.
sources.attribution: Fincham WNW, Brown LE, Roy HE, Dunn AM (2023). Interactive effects of resource quality and temperature drive differences in detritivory among native and invasive freshwater amphipods. Freshwater Biology 68(6):915-925. https://doi.org/10.1111/fwb.14075. Claim paraphrased.

claims.text: In laboratory microcosms, native Gammarus pulex processed leaf detritus faster than the two tested invasive Dikerogammarus species at the lower temperature treatments; the between-species differences decreased as the temperature treatments increased.
claims.placeTimeScope: Laboratory microcosms compared treatments at 8, 14, and 20 C using oak, sycamore, and alder leaf diets; paper published in 2023. These conditions describe the experiment and not the species' realized field ecology.
claims.lifeStatus: Experimental animals in laboratory microcosms; the result is not generalized to wild population rates or to other environmental conditions.

gaps: The laboratory comparison does not establish field detrital processing, natural population dynamics, responses across the full environmental range, or variation among G. pulex populations.

reasons: Only one bounded laboratory comparison of detrital processing has been assessed; six facets remain not-assessed.
The cited study is not a systematic review or complete account of the COL26.8 species concept.
No independent expert review has been completed.
